mechanism_narrative: The sharp fall in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES over the last two weeks indicates a continuing collapse in commuting and city-center trips, which will keep RETAIL_REC below its recent four-week average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days despite continued weakness in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM turns negative after being near baseline, it signals stronger household confinement and fewer routine shopping trips, which pulls RETAIL_REC lower within one week and keeps it weak for the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses below 0 after at least one week at or above 0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays above its prior four-week mean in the week after GROCERY_PHARM first turns negative.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL increases while PARKS and TRANSIT both fall, the same households are substituting away from discretionary outings and public movement, so RETAIL_REC will decline over the next two to four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 14 days when RESIDENTIAL is rising and both PARKS and TRANSIT are falling.

mechanism_narrative: A very large weekly drop in PARKS below the prior week's level identifies a broad mobility shock, and retail visitation will weaken over the following four weeks because discretionary trip generation is contracting across the city.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower than its last-28-day mean within four weeks of a >15-point weekly drop in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, simultaneous declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reduce weekday city-center exposure, so retail-and-recreation mobility should keep falling over the next two weeks rather than stabilizing.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or increases over the next 14 days while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue to decline.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains above 30 percentage points and TRANSIT stays below -60 percentage points, households are effectively substituting home time for outside trips, which will depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not remain below its prior 28-day average during periods when RESIDENTIAL exceeds 30 and TRANSIT is below -60.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after a steep decline indicates improved weather or weekend substitution toward outdoor activity, and that shift will support RETAIL_REC higher within one to two weeks as discretionary movement normalizes.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises after a week below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within two weeks after PARKS rebounds from below -25.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays near baseline while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES keep falling, essential trips are being preserved but discretionary city-center trips are collapsing, so RETAIL_REC should continue lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall over the next 28 days when GROCERY_PHARM is roughly stable but TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue to weaken.
